title: On the Expressive Power of Mixture-of-Experts for Structured Complex Tasks
summary: The triangular router has an endpoint tie defect in its pointwise construction. This leaves the essential-supremum and existential alternatives open; finite-width training plateaus do not establish an asymptotic expressivity obstruction.

problems.title: Integer interfaces do not identify a valid local expert
claim: Appendix B.2 infers a valid interval from the maximum of the triangular scores \(\tau_i(t)=(t-i+1)_++(t-i)_+-2(t-i+1/2)_+\). It then invokes the selected expert’s local approximation guarantee for arbitrary inputs.
analysis: At every integer interface all scores are zero. Take three exact affine experts \(g_1(t)=t\), \(g_2(t)=2t-1\), \(g_3(t)=3t-3\), each used on its corresponding unit interval. Their joined target is continuous. At \(t=2\), a lowest-index tie selects \(g_1(2)=2\), although both valid adjacent pieces give \(f(2)=3\). Local errors are zero but the constructed pointwise error is \(1\). A fixed score-only tie cannot select appropriate intervals at every endpoint.
result: The displayed pointwise assignment fails at interfaces. This null-set failure does not refute an essential-supremum bound or the existence of another valid router.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use affine nearest-center scores \(a_i(t)=2c_it-c_i^2\), where \(c_i=i-1/2\). They order the centers by distance; adjacent endpoint ties involve only intervals containing that endpoint. A constant feature implements the intercept in a linear gate.
problems.impact_rationale: The witness concerns endpoint handling in one proof construction; it does not establish loss of the main approximation advantage.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Finite training plateaus do not establish an approximation floor
problems.source_location: Section 6, PDF p.10, finite-width MoE experiment
claim: Section 6 interprets the plateau of a six-expert model over the tested widths as limited expressive power.
analysis: Set every expert equal to the same dense ReLU network \(g\). The top-one output is then \(g\) for every router decision, so this class contains the corresponding dense class. A finite optimization plateau cannot establish a positive asymptotic approximation-error floor for that containing class.
result: The observed table is not contradicted. A fixed-resource depth advantage remains compatible with this containment argument.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a scope clarification, not an independently demonstrated paper error.
problems.existing_correction_status: Scope clarification only; no author-paper repair or adoption is asserted.
